fluff.overview: The Armored Personnel Carrier is a ubiquitous ten-ton combat transport found in virtually every military force across the Inner Sphere and Periphery. Produced in three standard configurations -- hover, tracked, and wheeled -- these vehicles serve as the primary means of delivering infantry squads to and from the combat zone. The basic designs date back to the Star League era around 2500, with primitive predecessors operating as early as 2390, and production has continued without interruption for centuries. Their simplicity, low cost, and ease of manufacture ensure that every House military, mercenary command, and planetary militia fields them in quantity, making them among the most commonly encountered military vehicles in the galaxy.
fluff.capabilities:
The machine gun variant of the tracked APC removes the infantry compartment to mount three turret-mounted machine guns with a full ton of ammunition. With no troop-carrying capacity, this conversion serves as a dedicated anti-infantry patrol vehicle, using the tracked chassis's all-terrain capability to pursue enemy infantry across rough ground. The turret provides three-hundred-sixty-degree coverage, allowing the vehicle to engage threats from any direction.

Forty points of standard armor give the tracked MG variant substantially better protection than the hover MG conversion, allowing it to operate in closer proximity to enemy forces. The tracked drive system's ability to negotiate broken terrain makes this variant particularly effective in urban and jungle environments where hover vehicles cannot operate and wheeled vehicles struggle.
fluff.deployment: The tracked MG variant serves primarily with garrison forces and planetary militias for patrol and anti-infantry operations in rough terrain. Its combination of all-terrain mobility and concentrated machine gun fire makes it effective for operations in environments where hover and wheeled vehicles cannot operate, including dense urban areas, jungles, and mountainous regions.
fluff.history:
The armored personnel carrier concept predates the modern Star League designs by over a century. Primitive APCs first appeared around 2390, using civilian drive train components and petrochemical-powered internal combustion engines to deliver troops under fire. Though crude by later standards, these early carriers established the fundamental template -- a lightly armed, armored box on wheels, tracks, or a hoverskirt -- that would endure for centuries. The Age of War and the technological advances it brought rendered these primitive designs obsolete for front-line service, but they never fully disappeared, remaining in use with militia and paramilitary forces well into the thirty-first century.

The modern APC entered service around 2500, when Star League-era manufacturers standardized three motive configurations optimized for different operational environments. Production spread rapidly across the Inner Sphere, with virtually every military manufacturer offering some version of the basic design. During the Succession Wars, demand far outstripped supply, and APCs became one of the few military vehicles that even the most devastated economies could continue producing. Hundreds of local manufacturers emerged to fill the gap, many working from incomplete specifications or reverse-engineered examples.

The standard APC's enduring legacy owes as much to its limitations as its capabilities. Its minimal carrying capacity of a single infantry squad pushed militaries to develop heavier alternatives, while its thin armor and light armament drove the creation of numerous weapon-platform conversions. Militia commanders, unable to afford purpose-built combat vehicles, frequently stripped the infantry compartment to mount LRM or SRM launchers, creating improvised fire support vehicles. The Taurian Concordat and Marian Hegemony independently developed sensor-equipped hover variants for border patrol duties. One notable action occurred in 3034, when Overste-Lojtnant Illya Stroncek of the Lyran Commonwealth led a column of tracked APCs through Kurita lines on Last Frontier, evacuating three companies of wounded infantry under sustained fire and earning the Order of the Griffin for her actions.
